title: Composition and strict base change in logarithmic smoothness
statement: For locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], use log smooth and log etale in the chart sense of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Composites of log smooth morphisms are log smooth; log etale morphisms are log smooth; hence a log etale morphism followed by a log smooth morphism is log smooth. A strict base change of a log smooth morphism is log smooth, where strict means the source log structure is the log structure pulled back from the target. These properties can be checked on jointly surjective strict etale neighborhoods of source and target. For a nonempty coherent log ideal on an fs log scheme, its saturated log blowup, whenever it exists, is log etale. Finite saturated log blowup towers are therefore log etale.

source.place: VI 1.1--1.7 and 2.1--2.2; VIII 3.3.7--3.3.10 (saturated log blowup charts); X proof of 1.1, 1.3 and 1.8, pp.139,146--148. Chart properties used explicitly there; general log-smooth chart calculus is Kato 1988 Theorem 3.5, WANTED locally.

proof.text: By the unique-lifting implication in [lem-per-fs-log-infinitesimal-criterion], every log etale morphism has the existence property and local finite presentation, hence is log smooth. Identities are log etale: in the chart definition [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] use $P\xrightarrow{1}P$, with zero group kernel and cokernel and identity comparison. More generally a strict etale map is log etale: pull back each target chart $P$, use $P\xrightarrow{1}P$, and its comparison map is the given etale scheme map. The associated-log-structure universal property [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] identifies this with the source chart; restrictions to etale neighborhoods preserve the chart.

source.place: X 1.2 proof, chart criterion; VIII 3.3.4(ii), strict etale charts; agent lifting argument using Kato 3.3/3.5

proof.text: Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ be log smooth. Their underlying maps, and therefore their composite by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition], are locally of finite presentation. For a strict square-zero test $T_0\hookrightarrow T$ and maps $a:T_0\to X$, $b:T\to Z$, first lift $fa:T_0\to Y$ over $b$ etale locally on $T$, using the criterion for $g$. On each resulting $T_j$, lift $a|_{T_{0,j}}$ over the chosen $T_j\to Y$ using the criterion for $f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-first-order-thickening-base-change], the pulled-back immersion is a first order thickening, and pulled-back log structures still make the immersion strict. The composite family covers $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition]. The criterion now gives log smoothness of $gf$. If both maps are log etale, the criterion gives a unique global lift to $Y$ and then a unique global lift to $X$; any lift to $X$ must induce that lift to $Y$, so the composite has unique lifting and is log etale. This also proves the mixed composition assertion after Step 1.

source.place: X proof of 1.1, p.139 and 1.9(i), p.148; XVI 3.7, p.254 (composition); agent two-stage lifting argument

proof.text: For a strict $h:Y'\to Y$ and $f:X\to Y$, form the ordinary scheme product $X'=X\times_YY'$ with projections $p,q$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $M_{X'}=p^*M_X$, the associated log structure of $p^{-1}M_X\to\mathcal O_{X'}$. Strictness gives $M_{Y'}=h^*M_Y$; thus the map of log structures for $q$ is the pullback of that for $f$. This is a log fibre product: a compatible pair of log maps to $X,Y'$ has a unique underlying scheme map to $X'$ and a unique log map: locally send a chart germ $[q,u]$ to the given image of $q$ times the unit $u$. The defining relations hold because both maps preserve structure maps; uniqueness fixes chart elements and units. These maps agree on overlaps by uniqueness. Locally its log structure is associated to the pullback of any fs chart $Q$ of $X$, so it is fs. For clarity, on a stalk with ring $A'$ that associated chart is $Q\oplus_{\beta^{-1}(A'^\times)}A'^\times$; the original chart and this chart are related by adjoining the new units, which is precisely log pullback. Assume $f$ is locally of finite presentation, as every log smooth $f$ is by [lem-per-fs-log-infinitesimal-criterion]. Then $q$ is locally of finite presentation: affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R'$ of $X'$ have ring $A\otimes_RR'$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], finite presentation is preserved by scalar extension [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition], and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] is affine-local. Hence $X'$ is locally Noetherian over the locally Noetherian $Y'$ [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], so $p^*M_X$ is a log structure in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

source.place: VIII 3.3.5--3.3.6, chart base change and strictness; explicit universal-property verification

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is log smooth and $h$ strict, with the product of Step 3. By Step 3, the underlying $q$ is locally of finite presentation and $X'$ is a locally Noetherian fs log scheme. Given a strict square-zero test for $q$, project its map $T_0\to X'$ to $X$ and its map $T\to Y'$ to $Y$. The criterion for $f$ gives etale-local lifts $T_j\to X$ compatible with $T_j\to Y$. Pair each with the fixed $T_j\to Y'$: Step 3 gives a log map $T_j\to X'$ whose restriction is the prescribed map on $T_{0,j}$ by uniqueness of the pairing. Thus $q$ satisfies existence, so is log smooth by the criterion. If $f$ is log etale the lift to $X$ is unique globally, and pairing proves unique lifting for $q$, so strict base change also preserves log etaleness.

source.place: VIII 3.3.5--3.3.6; agent strict-base-change lifting argument using Kato 3.3/3.5

proof.text: Locality means strict etale squares $U_i\to X$, $V_i\to Y$ with compatible $f_i:U_i\to V_i$ and the $U_i$ jointly covering $X$. If each $f_i$ has the required charts, compose its chart-neighborhood maps with $U_i\to X$ and $V_i\to Y$. These are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and the source chart-neighborhoods cover $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition]. Strictness identifies all pulled-back log structures, so these same charts satisfy the definition for $f$ [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Conversely, factor $f_i$ through $X\times_YV_i$. The projection to $V_i$ has the desired logarithmic property by Step 4. The map $U_i\to X\times_YV_i$ is strict and etale: both $U_i$ and $X\times_YV_i$ are etale over $X$, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], and cancellation gives etaleness of the factor. Step 1 makes that factor log etale, and Step 2 proves the claim. This proves both the smooth and etale locality assertions; arbitrary target coverings are pulled back to covering families by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change].

source.place: VI 1.1 (etale-local charts); VIII 3.3.4(ii), 3.3.8 descent; explicit chart-family argument

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I$ be a nonempty coherent log ideal. On a strict etale affine chart with fs monoid $P$ and nonempty finite generating set $E\subset P$, [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] presents its saturated log blowup by the charts $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e^{\rm sat}])$, $e\in E$, with $(Q_e^{\rm sat})^{\rm gp}=P^{\rm gp}$. For each chart the map $P\to Q_e^{\rm sat}$ therefore has group kernel and cokernel zero, of order one, invertible everywhere. Its comparison with the fibre product in [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] is an isomorphism (on rings it is the identity on the displayed tensor product), hence is etale. Thus the chart definition and Step 5 give log etaleness globally. The constructed model and any saturated blowup in the statement are uniquely isomorphic: their universal properties give maps in both directions and force both composites to be identities [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Consequently the claim applies to whichever representative of the universal object is used.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11, pp.107--108 (saturated blowup charts and log etaleness)

proof.text: Induct on the finite length of a saturated log blowup tower [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The empty tower has identity composite, log etale by Step 1. For the induction step the last blowup is log etale by Step 6, and the composite of it with the preceding tower is log etale by the log-etale part of Step 2. This includes principal centers, whose universal blowup is the identity, and empty underlying schemes.

source.place: VIII 3.3.9--3.3.11 (towers); X 1.3, p.139 (application to saturated log blowup towers)

proof_origin.place: ILO VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11, X proof of 1.1 and 1.9, XVI 3.7; arguments spelled out using the Kato infinitesimal criterion, whose local document is WANTED.
